<translate>
<!--T:1-->
'''Raids''' are wave-based battles against an invading army. You trigger one by killing a marked '''scout''' at a raid site; after a short omen the army arrives in waves at your position, ending with its bosses. Survive every wave and everyone still fighting is rewarded; fall (or leave) and the raid is lost.
</translate>

<div class="dmz-cards">
{{Card|Red Ribbon Army Assault|<translate><!--T:77--> General Red's soldiers and robots, sent after you when you take out a Red Ribbon base's commander.</translate>}}
{{Card|Saiyan Assault|<translate><!--T:2--> Saiyan soldiers and elites from a crashed pod, ending with Oozarus.</translate>}}
{{Card|Frieza's Invasion|<translate><!--T:3--> Frieza's army on Namek, led by Cui, Dodoria, Zarbon and the Ginyu Force.</translate>}}
{{Card|Gomah's Army|<translate><!--T:4--> Gomah's soldiers in the Demon Realm, with Glorio, Majin Kuu and Majin Duu.</translate>}}
</div>

<translate>
<!--T:21-->
All four raids have 5 waves. '''Hero of the World''' is a DMZ effect that boosts the TP you earn (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Effects|Effects]]).
</translate>

<translate>
== How a raid plays out == <!--T:22-->

<!--T:23-->
# '''Find a raid site.''' Red Ribbon bases, Saiyan Craters, Namekian Ruins and [[Special:MyLanguage/Gomah|Gomah]] Camps generate as structures (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Structures|Structures]]). When you come within 80 blocks of one, you get a chat warning, for example ''"Your scouter picks up a Saiyan pod that just crashed nearby..."''. Each site has one scout, shown with a supervillain aura; at a Red Ribbon base the scout is the base's commander, guarded by a garrison of soldiers and robots. A site is spent once its scout dies or disappears.
# '''Kill the scout.''' The player who kills it (or the nearest player, if nobody gets the credit) receives the '''Hunted''' effect and the preparation music starts. Hunted lasts the raid's preparation time (60 seconds by default). If the effect is removed early, for example by drinking milk, the raid is called off.
# '''The raid starts''' where you stand when Hunted runs out. The '''participants''' are you plus every member of your party (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Commands|Commands]]). Only one raid can run in the same area at a time.
# '''Waves.''' Enemies appear around the raid centre, 6–16 blocks out: story fighters drop in from above, while mobs that only walk, such as the Red Ribbon soldiers and robots, spawn on the ground. A boss bar shows ''"Raid — Wave X/Y — N left"''; it turns purple on boss waves. Raid mobs glow so they're easy to find: minions in purple, bosses in red. In waves with bosses, the bosses stay '''dormant''' until their escort is dead, but attacking one wakes it up early. There's a short pause between waves (5 seconds by default).
# '''Victory.''' When the last wave is cleared, every participant still fighting gets the rewards, the victory music, fireworks and the ''Hero of the World'' effect.
# '''Defeat.''' A participant who dies, logs out, changes dimension or switches to spectator is out. Walking farther than 80 blocks (by default) from the raid centre gives you a 15-second countdown to come back. When no participant is left, the raid is lost: the remaining mobs vanish and every participant sees '''YOU LOST!''' and loses alignment (see the table above and [[Special:MyLanguage/Alignment|Alignment]]).
</translate>

<translate>
=== Difficulty === <!--T:24-->

<!--T:25-->
Raid mobs' health and damage are multiplied by the '''story difficulty''' of the player who started the raid, using the Easy and Hard health and damage multipliers of the server (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Sagas|Sagas]] for the difficulties).
</translate>

{{Config|General Server Config|gameplay}}

<translate>
== Commands == <!--T:26-->

<!--T:27-->
All <code>/dmzraid</code> subcommands require operator permission level 2.
</translate>
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:28--> Command</translate> !! <translate><!--T:29--> What it does</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmzraid start [type]}} || <translate><!--T:30--> Starts a raid of that type at your position: <code>red_ribbon_assault</code>, <code>saiyan_assault</code> (the default), <code>frieza_invasion</code>, <code>gomah_assault</code> or an extra raid. Fails if a raid is already running nearby.</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmzraid stop}} || <translate><!--T:31--> Cancels the nearest raid within 128 blocks (no defeat penalty).</translate>
|-
| {{Command|/dmzraid info}} || <translate><!--T:32--> Shows the nearest raid's id, status, wave, participant count and centre.</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Configuration == <!--T:33-->

<!--T:34-->
Raids are defined in JSON files under <code>config/dragonminez/raids/</code>, so server owners can tune the shipped raids or add their own. Each raid is one file named after its id: <code>red_ribbon_assault.json</code>, <code>saiyan_assault.json</code>, <code>frieza_invasion.json</code> and <code>gomah_assault.json</code> are generated with their defaults and version-updated like the other config files. Any other <code>.json</code> file in the folder is loaded as an '''extra raid''' with the file name as its id; files whose name starts with <code>old_</code> are ignored. Reload with <code>/dmzreload config</code>.
</translate>

{{See also|Reloading and Updating Changes|How to JSON}}

<translate>
=== Top-level fields === <!--T:35-->
</translate>
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:36--> Field</translate> !! <translate><!--T:37--> Type</translate> !! <translate><!--T:38--> Default</translate> !! <translate><!--T:39--> Notes</translate>
|-
| <code>configVersion</code> || String || — || <translate><!--T:40--> Managed by DMZ.</translate>
|-
| <code>enabled</code> || Boolean || <code>true</code> || <translate><!--T:41--> <code>false</code> removes the raid.</translate>
|-
| <code>displayName</code> || String || <code>raid.dragonminez.&lt;id&gt;</code> || <translate><!--T:42--> Translation key shown on the boss bar.</translate>
|-
| <code>activationRadius</code> || Number || <code>48</code> || <translate><!--T:43--> No second raid can start within this distance of a running one; also the range used to credit a scout kill to the nearest player.</translate>
|-
| <code>leashDistance</code> || Number || <code>80</code> || <translate><!--T:44--> How far participants can go from the raid centre before the 15-second countdown.</translate>
|-
| <code>interWaveDelaySeconds</code> || Integer || <code>5</code> || <translate><!--T:45--> Pause between waves.</translate>
|-
| <code>music</code> || Object || — || <translate><!--T:46--> <code>preparation</code> (sound event played during the omen) and <code>battle</code> (played during the waves; default <code>dragonminez:raid_ost_1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>trigger</code> || Object || — || <translate><!--T:47--> How the raid is started (see below). A raid without a trigger can only be started with <code>/dmzraid start</code>.</translate>
|-
| <code>waves</code> || List || — || <translate><!--T:48--> The waves, in order. A raid with no waves is skipped.</translate>
|-
| <code>rewards</code> || Object || — || <translate><!--T:49--> <code>trainingPoints</code>, <code>effects</code> (<code>id</code>, <code>seconds</code>, <code>amplifier</code>) and <code>items</code> (<code>id</code>, <code>count</code>), given to every participant still fighting at the end.</translate>
|-
| <code>defeat</code> || Object || — || <translate><!--T:50--> <code>title</code> and <code>subtitle</code> (translation keys) and <code>alignment</code> (signed alignment change applied to every participant).</translate>
|}

<translate>
=== Trigger === <!--T:51-->
</translate>
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:52--> Field</translate> !! <translate><!--T:53--> Type</translate> !! <translate><!--T:54--> Notes</translate>
|-
| <code>entityId</code> || String || <translate><!--T:55--> The scout: an entity id, or an entity tag with <code>#</code> (for example <code>#dragonminez:frieza_soldiers</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>dimension</code> || String || <translate><!--T:56--> Dimension the trigger works in.</translate>
|-
| <code>spawnChance</code> || Number (0–1) || <translate><!--T:57--> Chance that a '''naturally spawned''' mob matching <code>entityId</code> in that dimension is marked as a raid scout. <code>0</code> in all shipped raids, which rely on their raid sites instead.</translate>
|-
| <code>supervillain</code> || Boolean || <translate><!--T:58--> Show the scout with the supervillain aura (default <code>true</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>preparationSeconds</code> || Integer || <translate><!--T:59--> Length of the omen (default <code>60</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>announceMessage</code>, <code>omenMessage</code>, <code>startMessage</code> || String || <translate><!--T:60--> Translation keys for the raid-site warning, the omen and the start of the raid.</translate>
|-
| <code>health</code>, <code>meleeDamage</code>, <code>kiDamage</code>, <code>aiTier</code> || Number || <translate><!--T:61--> Stats of the scout placed at a raid site.</translate>
|}

<translate>
<!--T:62-->
The structure raid sites (Red Ribbon base, Saiyan Crater, Namekian Ruins and Gomah Camp) are tied to the four shipped raids. An extra raid can use <code>spawnChance</code> or <code>/dmzraid start</code>.
</translate>

<translate>
=== Waves === <!--T:63-->

<!--T:64-->
Each wave is <code>{ "spawns": [ ... ] }</code>, and each spawn entry describes one group:
</translate>
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate><!--T:65--> Field</translate> !! <translate><!--T:66--> Type</translate> !! <translate><!--T:67--> Notes</translate>
|-
| <code>entityId</code> || String || <translate><!--T:68--> Entity id, or <code>#tag</code> to pick a random member of an entity tag for each mob.</translate>
|-
| <code>count</code> || Integer || <translate><!--T:69--> How many to spawn (default <code>1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>health</code>, <code>meleeDamage</code>, <code>kiDamage</code> || Number || <translate><!--T:70--> Absolute stats, before the difficulty multiplier.</translate>
|-
| <code>aiTier</code> || Integer || <translate><!--T:71--> <code>1</code> Novice, <code>2</code> Smart, <code>3</code> Elite, <code>4</code> Expert.</translate>
|-
| <code>textureVariant</code> || Integer || <translate><!--T:72--> Texture variant, for mobs that have several.</translate>
|-
| <code>dormantUntilEscortDead</code> || Boolean || <translate><!--T:73--> Boss behaviour: the mob waits until the rest of the wave is dead.</translate>
|-
| <code>canTransform</code> || Boolean || <translate><!--T:74--> Whether the mob may transform (default <code>true</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>transformHealth</code>, <code>transformMeleeDamage</code>, <code>transformKiDamage</code> || Number || <translate><!--T:75--> Stats of the transformed form.</translate>
|}

<translate>
<!--T:76-->
Example: the first two waves of Frieza's Invasion.
</translate>
<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
"waves": [
  { "spawns": [ { "entityId": "#dragonminez:frieza_soldiers", "count": 5,  "health": 100, "meleeDamage": 15, "kiDamage": 10, "aiTier": 1 } ] },
  { "spawns": [ { "entityId": "#dragonminez:frieza_soldiers", "count": 10, "health": 130, "meleeDamage": 18, "kiDamage": 12, "aiTier": 1 } ] }
]
</syntaxhighlight>
